questions.prompt: The modern periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing…
Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: A vertical column: same number of outer electrons
A horizontal row: same number of shells
Element with properties between metals and non-metals

questions.prompt: Element X has electron arrangement 2, 8, 3. Where is it on the periodic table?
questions.explain: 3 shells = period 3; 3 outer electrons = group 13. It's aluminium.
Metals on the left, non-metals on the right, metalloids along the staircase.

questions.prompt: Why do elements in the same group have similar chemical properties?
options: They have the same number of outer electrons
They have the same number of shells
questions.explain: Chemical properties depend on outer electrons.

questions.prompt: What made Mendeleev's periodic table so impressive?
options: He left gaps and correctly predicted the properties of undiscovered elements
questions.explain: A good scientific model makes predictions that are later confirmed.

questions.prompt: Chlorine is in group 17. How many electrons are in its outer shell?
questions.explain: For groups 13–18, outer electrons = group number − 10. 17 − 10 = 7.

questions.text: There are ___ known elements today. Metals are found on the ___ side of the periodic table.
questions.explain: 118 elements; metals on the left, non-metals on the right.

questions.prompt: Rubidium is below potassium in group 1. Predict two of its properties and explain your reasoning.
questions.modelAnswer: Rubidium will be a soft, shiny metal with 1 outer electron, like other group 1 metals. It will react even more vigorously with water than potassium, because reactivity increases down group 1 (the outer electron is further from the nucleus and lost more easily).
rubric: Predicted it is a metal / has 1 outer electron
Predicted it is more reactive than potassium
Explained using the group trend or electron arrangement
questions.explain: Patterns in the periodic table let you predict properties.
